subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation mode, and if so should the permanent policy be interactive confirmation, static allow/block lists, temporary grants, or part of a broader SSRF policy surface?
rationale: The source has the low-level allow/block primitives, but choosing approval UX, grant lifetime, metadata hard-block semantics, and public config shape changes a security boundary that automation should not decide.

options.title: Design Browser SSRF Approval Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the browser-scoped confirmation, allowlist/blocklist, timeout, audit, and metadata-deny semantics before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader SSRF Policy
options.body: Make this request wait for a global or shared SSRF policy design that also covers web_fetch, providers, channels, and auth-refresh paths.

options.title: Keep Current Strict/Broad Toggle Model
options.body: Decline confirmation mode for now and keep the current strict default plus explicit dangerous opt-in and hostname exceptions.

recommendation.title: Design Browser SSRF Approval Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the browser-scoped confirmation, allowlist/blocklist, timeout, audit, and metadata-deny semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for browser SSRF config, shared SSRF guards, and security docs points to this account.
